title: RETFound: Self-Supervised Retinal Foundation Model for Ocular & Systemic Disease
whyItMatters: First open-source self-supervised foundation model in medical imaging—pretrained on 1.6 million unlabeled retinal scans—accurately diagnosing sight-threatening eye diseases and forecasting heart failure, stroke, and Parkinson’s disease.
summary: Yukun Zhou, Mark Chia, Siegfried Wagner, Pearse Keane, and colleagues (UCL & Moorfields Eye Hospital) introduced RETFound in Nature (2023), demonstrating how masked-autoencoder self-supervised pretraining on 1.6 million unlabeled clinical retinal photographs and OCT scans overcomes medical AI’s chronic label bottleneck. When fine-tuned on small labeled cohorts, RETFound outperformed supervised baselines across diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and macular degeneration while predicting 3-year systemic incidence of heart failure, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, and Parkinson’s disease from noninvasive eye scans alone.
technicalHighlights: Self-supervised ViT-Large masked autoencoder pretrained on 904,170 color fundus photographs and 736,442 OCT scans from Moorfields Eye Hospital.
Required up to 10× fewer expert clinical labels than supervised models while generalizing robustly across external international and multi-ethnic cohorts.
Launched "oculomics" foundation modeling by predicting systemic cardiovascular and neurodegenerative diseases (including Parkinson’s) directly from retinal imagery.
caveats: Systemic-disease AUCs (0.67–0.79) serve as risk-enrichment biomarkers rather than standalone diagnostic tests, and clinical deployment requires prospective validation and demographic fairness auditing.
institutions: Moorfields Eye Hospital NHS Foundation Trust

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved that self-supervised foundation pretraining unlocks label-efficient generalist medical imaging across ocular and systemic biology.
scoreRationale.ripple: Open weights sparked hundreds of clinical medical foundation models across pathology, radiology, and oculomics.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Nature with multi-cohort international external validation and open-source model weights.
scoreRationale.velocity: Reduced specialist clinical annotation requirements by an order of magnitude for rare and systemic disease tasks.
